title: Technological Convergence Bottlenecks
definition: The multi-faceted barriers preventing the creation of an ideal, multi-purpose technological component.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine trying to make a perfect sandwich that's both crunchy and sweet. You face challenges like finding the right ingredients and the right balance of flavors. In technology, these 'challenges' are called bottlenecks, and they're what's stopping us from building the perfect product.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Technological convergence bottlenecks are the interconnected obstacles that hinder the development of a single, high-performance technology by requiring expertise in various fields, such as physics, materials science, and manufacturing.
difficulty_levels.expert: Technological convergence bottlenecks are a complex interplay of physical constraints, market demands, and technological limitations. They can be considered the edges of our current knowledge and capabilities, pushing us to explore new materials and manufacturing techniques to overcome them.

extra_fields.insight: Understanding the various bottlenecks that hinder the development of a single, high-performance technology can help in identifying potential solutions and fostering innovation.
